data.narrative:
Code Metal, a Series B defense and security company founded by Peter Morales and Alex Showalter-Bucher, is currently valued at $1.25B post-money following $161M in total capital raised. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 companies across Defense & Security at matching or proximate stages: 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Castelion ($1.0B), Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), and Heven AeroTech ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the current $1.2B post-money valuation and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies $2.4B. Peer-median analysis across the 6 same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B. The peer set reflects material dispersion, consistent with heterogeneous risk profiles within frontier defense technology.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated valuation range of $850M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.7B. The current $1.25B valuation falls in the lower-to-middle portion of this range. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to Dream Security and Harmattan AI at the upper end, execution risk in a capital-intensive sector, and regulatory pathway clarity. The wide peer range ($300M–$3.0B) underscores stage and commercial maturity as material drivers of valuation variance within this cohort.
